name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 201 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata.
status.nb: 201 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Kolkata.

summary.en: Lateef Bhat, a Lashkar-e-Taiba commander, was killed in a Kulgam encounter and his weapon recovered, while a military vehicle plunged into the Itam River in Manipur, killing an army captain and seriously injuring three soldiers; the Manipur governor and chief minister paid tribute to the fallen personnel. A government employee was killed in a road accident in Shopian and another was hit-and-run in South Kashmir, prompting the Kulgam CMO to terminate two security guards for dereliction of duty. A senior police officer died after a boulder fell on him in an Anantnag forest. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Lateef Bhat, en Lashkar-e-Taiba-kommandør, ble drept i et oppgjør i Kulgam, og våpenet hans ble funnet, mens et militært kjøretøy styrtet i Itam-elven i Manipur, og drepte en hærkaptein og påførte alvorlige skader på tre soldater; guvernøren og statsministeren i Manipur hedret det falne personellet. En offentlig ansatt ble drept i en veitrafikkulykke i Shopian, og en annen ble påkjørt og forlatt i Sør-Kashmir, noe som fikk Kulgam CMO til å avskjedige to sikkerhetsvakter for tjenesteunndragelse. En senior politioffiser døde etter at en stein falt på ham i en skog i Anantnag. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
